description: Maps the formal TLA+ model (KvResidencyPool.tla) actions to actual Rust call sites and the broker integration boundary. Each seam is a point where the formal model's abstraction boundary meets real source code.

callers.trigger: After a successful provider completion, observe_kv derives LeaseDemand from the response's usage.prompt_tokens and calls kv.acquire.

seams.source_guard: occupied_units + incoming <= capacity (with rollback: previous lease is restored on capacity refusal; reclaim is triggered)
seams.abstraction_gap: The model uses 1 unit per context; source uses variable units derived from prompt_tokens. The model does not model the rollback-on-failure path (restoring the previous lease).

callers.trigger: Before dispatching a request to the provider, a read hold is taken on the context whose KV may be reused.

seams.model_guard: state in {Resident, ReclaimPending, Transferring}; readers < MaxReaders
seams.source_guard: state in {Resident, ReclaimPending, Transferring}; ReclaimPending is revived to Resident
seams.abstraction_gap: Source has no explicit MaxReaders bound; the model bound is for TLC finiteness.

callers.trigger: After the provider completes (terminal 200, 429, or error), end_read drains the read hold taken at dispatch.

seams.source_guard: readers > 0; lease_revision incremented; if readers reaches 0 and state in {ReclaimPending, Invalid}: lease removed

callers.trigger: When the provider connection dies without a response (DropWithoutResponse / timeout), the read hold is converted to an unknown-read hold instead of being released.

seams.source_guard: request not already held; context has a lease with readers > 0
seams.note: The pool never invents occupancy: only a context that already had a reader can be held.

callers.trigger: When the original terminal evidence for an unknown request arrives (429, durable error, or late success), release_unknown_read drains the held reader.

seams.model_guard: unknownReads[r] != none; drain_reader on the held context
seams.source_guard: the hold exists in unknown_reads; the context_id is looked up and drain_reader is called

callers.function: Not directly called by broker dispatch; called by rebalance/reclaim indirectly or by explicit pool cleanup
callers.note: The broker handle exposes no raw release entry point. Release happens through reclaim (eviction) or through explicit pool management during identity changes.

seams.model_guard: present; !HasUnknownRead; if readers=0: remove, else: ReclaimPending
seams.source_guard: has_unknown_read check returns Err(UnresolvedUnknownRead); readers > 0 moves to ReclaimPending

callers.trigger: Called after plan application during rebalance. Also called during acquire when the context doesn't fit.
The broker periodically rebalances, which triggers reclaim if occupied > capacity.

seams.source_guard: Same guards plus ordering by return_probability, priority, recompute_units
seams.abstraction_gap: The model nondeterministically picks any eligible context; source uses a deterministic ordering.

callers.trigger: After a successful capability probe (GET /v1/models + GET /metrics), the broker adopts the new identity and invalidates stale handles.

seams.model_guard: newId != poolIdentity; all non-matching leases set to Invalid
seams.abstraction_gap: Source identity has 6 optional fields with option-compatible matching; model uses single-tag equality.

callers.function: observe_kv (when context already has a lease)
callers.trigger: When acquire is called for a context that already has a lease, the lease is updated in place.

seams.source_guard: previous lease is removed, new lease is built from the old one with updated demand/identity, then re-inserted

integration_boundary.pool_ownership: The pool state (KvPoolState) is owned by ResourceDomain and accessed through &mut self methods. The KvAllocator borrows the pool mutably for each operation. No concurrent access is possible at the Rust level.
integration_boundary.broker_dispatch_lifecycle: execute_request (execution.rs) is the single entry point: it calls begin_read before dispatch, observe_kv after success, hold_unknown_read on unknown outcome, and end_read on all terminal paths. The broker's reconcile_recorded handles late terminal evidence for unknown reads.
integration_boundary.capability_probe_lifecycle: BrokerHandle::probe_capabilities (broker.rs) drives GET /v1/models + GET /metrics, then adopt_capabilities -> adopt_identity + apply_capabilities + rebalance.
cross_owner_needs: RefillBrokerWiring1106 owns the WindowLimits/effective-window path; this slice exposes Option<u64> backend pool observation for parent integration
Parent owns Cargo.toml, lib.rs module wiring, integration tests
